title: The normal endpoint of the Cartesian-centre span
statement: Assume additionally that h≫aY is separated. For the setting and any common Cartesian-centre span D of lem-pur-diagonal-etale-cartesian-centre-span, inverse normal restriction along D.left, normal restriction along D.right, and inverse normal base comparison compose to the independently constructed normal comparison along the actual Rees-normal map. No DNC comparison delta, orientation, or dualizing comparison is part of this assertion.

proof.text: The normal maps of both etale maps in D are isomorphisms over U. Compose their Rees maps and use D.factorization. Restrict to zero and cancel the closed zero-fibre inclusion to identify the resulting normal map with the actual normalMap.

Apply restriction/base-change compatibility to a section-pair isomorphism and the identity pair map. The identity restriction and identity base comparison, and naturality of the pullback unit, identify restriction with inverse smooth exchange. Paste the two isomorphism squares with the actual normal base square. Base comparison composition and the equality from the first step cancel the intermediate comparisons, giving precisely normal. Rank zero and the empty base obey the same equations.

lean.statement:
theorem span_normal_endpoint (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {U X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (d : ℕ) (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d g]
    (h : U ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated h] [LocallyOfFiniteType h] [QuasiCompact h]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d h]
    (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType aY] [QuasiCompact aY]
    [IsSeparated (h ≫ aY)]
    (e : U ⟶ X) [Etale e] (w : e ≫ g = h)
    (D : CentreSpan d g h e w) :
    (restriction P (h ≫ aY) (normalEtaleMap P (h ≫ aY) D.left)).symm ≪≫
        restriction P (h ≫ aY) (normalEtaleMap P (h ≫ aY) D.right) ≪≫
        (baseComparison P (g ≫ aY) (h ≫ aY)
          (normalBaseChange P (g ≫ aY) (h ≫ aY) (baseSquare d g e))).symm =
      normal P d g h aY e w
